answer: A bonded-stake registry is the main Sybil brake. To list an agent, an operator locks collateral on a public ledge of epoch records; every signed answer is charged against that stake, and provably correlated aliases or votes against consensus get the collateral burned and the seat revoked. Each fake identity needs real capital at risk, so a thousand sybils cost a thousand stakes. Attack cost scales with identities while expected payout stays flat, which removes the profit. Like a lotus opening from mud, a new agent must prove skin in the game before earning a violet reputation score.
